To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cancer education programs should identify the patient's knowledge of cancer, 2) elicit and respectfully discuss beliefs about cancer, 3) provide cancer information in a language that the patient can understand.

(1) cancer knowledge was low in a group of Vietnamese and Cambodians living in Philadelphia, (2) cancer knowledge increased with age, (3) employment and education were related to cancer knowledge, (4) length of time in this country did not affect cancer knowledge.
(1) 70% of the Southeast Asian women interviewed did not know what a cancer was; and (2) 74% of the women were unable to identify cancer prevention strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cancer prevention in the Vietnamese and Cambodian communities in the United States.
cancer screening and prevention behaviors among women of Southeast Asian origin in the United States.
the identification of the knowledge and beliefs of a group of Southeast Asian women regarding cancer and the development of culturally appropriate educational interventions for these populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cancer screening is a very complex issue that involves a number of different factors.
cancer knowledge in Southeast Asian women is low and is associated with employment status and education level.
the majority of Southeast Asian women in this study had a low level of cancer knowledge and did not engage in cancer prevention behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found low levels of knowledge about cancer and cancer prevention strategies among Vietnamese and Cambodian immigrant women living in Philadelphia.
the majority of women in this study were not knowledgeable about cancer.
we have identified the need for cancer prevention education programs for this population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer education programs need to be culturally and linguistically tailored to address the unique health beliefs and needs of Southeast Asian women.
we should not make any assumptions about a patient’s knowledge about cancer, especially in a culturally diverse population.
cancer education programs need to be tailored to meet the needs of the patient and to address their beliefs about cancer and prevention.
